title: Terraform UEBA alert definitions: accepted names and lookups

prose.text: {{docs-security-ueba-category}} Both the resource and the data source are strict about how an alert is named. The accepted names are fixed in the provider.

checks.do: Whether a rejected `alert_name` is outside the provider's fixed list, which is not proof the backend lacks that alert.
Whether a data source lookup by alert name matched exactly, including case.

alert-name-closed-list.statement: The `alert_name` of `zia_ueba_alert_definitions` is validated, case-sensitively, against a fixed list of alert names compiled into the provider; a name outside that list fails validation at plan time.

quotes: "alert_name": { Type: schema.TypeString, Required: true, ValidateFunc: validation.StringInSlice(supportedUEBAAlertNames, false),

list-is-provider-boundary.statement: So the closed list is what Terraform accepts, not evidence that the backend's alert catalog is the same set or that every listed alert is enabled for every tenant.
list-is-provider-boundary.conditions: Inferred from the list being a constant in the provider; no source ties it to the backend's catalog.

data-source-selectors.statement: The UEBA alert definitions data source needs an `id` or an `alert_name`, matches the name by exact case-sensitive equality over the full list, and fails with "either 'id' or 'alert_name' must be provided" when neither is given.

import-by-id-or-name.statement: The resource imports by a numeric definition ID or, when the import ID is not numeric, by alert name through a by-name lookup.

quotes: idInt, parseIDErr := strconv.ParseInt(id, 10, 64) if parseIDErr == nil { _ = d.Set("alert_definition_id", idInt) } else { resp, err := alert_definitions.GetByName(ctx, service, id)

docs-security-ueba-category.statement: The provider documents `zia_ueba_alert_definitions` under the "Security & UEBA Alerts" subcategory, as a resource that creates and manages a ZIA Security & UEBA alert definition.

quotes: Creates and manages a ZIA Security & UEBA alert definition.
